name: Dynamic DNS
overview: Keep your DNS records pointed at your server's current public IP.
description: Keeps one or more DNS records pointed at your Jellyfin server's current public IP. Runs entirely in-process as a scheduled task and updates your DNS provider over outbound HTTP/S. Great for anyone who wants to run their entire stack entirely through Jellyfin without external programs or dependencies.

versions.changelog:
## Changed
- Configuration says less. Each step states where it stands in one short line, and descriptions no longer repeat it.
- Links to Advanced read as Advanced > Blocking, Advanced > Addresses and so on, the same way across the plugin.
- Step 6 no longer repeats the time of the outside check, which its card already shows.

## Developer
- The Beginner's Guide has Free and Recommended tabs. Picking one switches every tab on the page, so only your path shows.
- The docs use the same Advanced > Blocking style as the plugin, with new screenshots.

## Added
- The top of Configuration shows how many of the six steps are done, with a bar for each step and a link to the next one that needs attention.
- Configuration names the countries that can connect, in green, or says in yellow that the server's country is not known yet. A link goes straight to the country rule.
- The share card has Copy URL and Copy Image. Copy Image puts the QR code on the clipboard, or saves it as a file where the browser cannot copy images.

## Changed
- A server now keeps one DDNS record, and its hostname is the proxy's address. Step 2 asks only for the provider, the hostname and the credentials that provider needs. Saving with older extra records keeps only the one shown.
- Configuration has one Save for the whole page, and the steps use smaller buttons with the same spacing throughout.
- The finer settings moved to Advanced. Dynamic DNS holds the record's options and Remove Record. Addresses holds Other addresses and Automatic port forwarding. Security holds Request a New Certificate.
- The share card shows a Public or Home only badge, with a note pointing to step 2 when the address only works at home.
- On Advanced, the server's country in the country rule is shown in green, or in yellow while it is unknown.

## Developer
- The docs explain the defaults worth knowing, the single record and the new Advanced sections, with new screenshots.

## Added
- Automatic port forwarding. Remote Access asks your router to forward ports 80 and 443 through UPnP or NAT-PMP, keeps the forward renewed and removes it when Jellyfin stops. It never takes over a forward that belongs to another device.
- CGNAT detection. The Router step tells you when your provider shares one internet address between customers, so forwarded ports cannot be reached.
- A name check that shows whether your address points at this server's public IP.
- Test from Outside checks that your address can be reached from other countries.
- The Dashboard opens with a QR code and link to your server, with Copy and Share buttons.

## Changed
- Setup, Domains, Address and Proxy are now one Configuration tab with six numbered steps. Each step shows whether it is done and holds its own settings.
- The IP detection and update settings from the Address tab are now under Advanced, Dynamic DNS.
- Remote Access now proxies Jellyfin only. Services are removed, and other apps are best served by NGINX, Apache or SWAG.

## Developer
- The docs cover the new tabs, port forwarding, CGNAT and the outside test, with new screenshots.

## Fixed
- INWX, ClouDNS and Directnic records can be saved again. They have no hostname field, and saving no longer asks for one.
- Saving or deleting a record on the Domains tab changes only that record, so a cleared record is never deleted and other records' unsaved edits or newer changes are never overwritten.
- With Only through the proxy on, if the proxy fails to start, Jellyfin gets its own addresses back and the setting is turned off, so the server stays reachable. A save or Restart Proxy can no longer leave the proxy stopped while Jellyfin listens only through it.
- Trust the Proxy, Undo and saves no longer run over each other, so Jellyfin's original network settings are always kept for Undo.
- A record deleted at the DNS provider is put back, and a GoDaddy record for the domain itself is written to the domain instead of a doubled name.
- When one address family keeps failing, the record now backs off and only that family is retried, instead of logging an error every 15 minutes.
- Let's Encrypt's DNS check no longer fails on networks that block DNS-over-HTTPS, and a certificate that cannot be loaded is not ordered again straight away.
- Domains and Address show the server's reason when a save fails, and every tab warns before leaving with unsaved changes.
- The warning when visitors look local now also catches setups where only some visitors are hidden, such as IPv6 through Docker.

## Changed
- One address block can no longer hold more than a small share of the proxy's connections or requests, and HTTP/2 streams per connection are capped, so a few addresses cannot crowd out everyone else.
- Repeat bans on a whole IPv6 network last longer each time, and saved bans apply from the first connection after a restart.
- Services no longer receive login headers sent by visitors, and a Service that points at Jellyfin itself is refused.
- Provider notes are at most two sentences, and several provider messages are plainer.

## Developer
- The docs fix every finding from an audit against the code, and there are now two Beginner's Guides, a free one with Duck DNS and a recommended one with your own domain.

## Changed
- The Compression setting on the Advanced tab is removed. Jellyfin already compresses its own pages through the proxy, so the proxy compressing them again was wasted work. Web assets now serve about 7% faster through HTTPS. Compression for other apps is still set on each Service.

## Fixed
- When the Domains tab cannot load its settings, it now says so even when there are no records yet.
- Correcting a server clock that had run ahead no longer forgets when the current Let's Encrypt certificate was issued.

## Developer
- A cleanup sweep removed unused code, merged duplicated helpers in the pages and the server code, and fixed stale comments.
- The pages are embedded with one pattern instead of a list, and build.sh no longer checks a partial list of them.
- The unused slash-command workflows are removed.
- The docs add a Dashboard page under Features, and the Beginner's Guide starts by checking for CGNAT.

## Changed
- The Request a New Certificate scheduled task is removed. Refresh Certificate already requests a new certificate whenever one is missing, no longer covers your addresses, or expires within 30 days. To force one now, use Request a New Certificate on the Proxy tab.
- The Update Dynamic DNS scheduled task is now Update DDNS, and Update Location Database is now Refresh Locations. Their schedules carry over.

## Changed
- Every field description on every tab is one short sentence, two at most, with units and defaults kept.
- Each provider's note under the Provider list names the fields exactly as the form shows them.
- Long confirmations and warnings, such as the one for every visitor looking local, are shorter.
- The Advanced tab no longer shows the line about every setting starting on its default.

## Fixed
- The Minimum read rate description says what it limits, how slowly a visitor reads pages, not uploads.
- The IP detection description no longer says the services are tried in order until one answers, since two must agree.

## Developer
- The documentation is rewritten, with a Beginner's Guide from buying a domain to remote access in one page, a Settings Reference listing every setting with its default, and a page per tab.
- Provider pages list only the fields each provider shows, named as on screen.

## Added
- Remote Access, a secure HTTPS proxy in front of Jellyfin on ports 80 and 443, with Let's Encrypt, your own certificate files, or a self-signed certificate from the plugin's own root that devices install once.
- Trust the Proxy, which lets Jellyfin see each visitor's real address while keeping its own ports, and Undo, which puts its settings back. Only through the proxy, an opt-in Advanced setting, makes the proxy the only way in.
- Protection for internet visitors, with bans for failed sign-ins on the address and its wider IPv6 networks, a block list, country rules, sign-in limits and connection caps.
- Services, so other apps on your network such as a request manager can be reached through the proxy on their own address.
- A Dashboard with a world map, bans and a history of who connected, signed in or was turned away. Locations come from DB-IP.
- The Proxy tab warns when every visitor looks local, as behind rootless Docker or a tunnel, where bans and country rules cannot work.

## Changed
- The project and its repository are now Remote Access, at JPKribs/jellyfin-plugin-remoteaccess. Existing records and settings carry over.
- Logging is quieter. A problem that repeats is logged once, with a line when it clears, and a failed DNS update is a warning when DNS still serves the right address.

## Fixed
- Blank records are no longer saved, a failed delete puts the record back, and unsaved edits survive switching records.
- FreeDNS update links are only followed back to FreeDNS itself.

## Developer
- Built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0). Servers on Jellyfin 12.0 or 12.1 keep the previous release.
- CodeQL runs in this repository and leaves compiler-generated code out of its results.

## Developer
- Built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0). Servers on Jellyfin 12.0 or 12.1 keep the previous release.
- Updated test dependencies (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11, NSubstitute 6.2, xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1).

## Fixed
- Timeouts, network errors, rate limits, and provider server errors no longer pause a record for the full backoff window after three failures; they earn a short pause that starts at 15 minutes and doubles up to 2 hours, and only a sustained run of them takes the full window. Rejected credentials and requests still use the full window.
- A paused record is retried as soon as the public IP changes, so a pause never holds back a new address.
- Editing a record's provider, hostname, zone, server, or credentials resets its status, so it no longer inherits the old target's pause and last pushed address.
- When one address family times out, the other family's successful update is still recorded.
- A malformed IP detection URL fails on its own instead of aborting the whole update run, and detection replies are read with a size cap.
- The live DNS check resolves the record's real name (the hostname completed with its zone, or the DuckDNS domain) and is skipped for numeric record IDs and several DuckDNS labels instead of resolving them as addresses.
- Run now keeps running when you navigate away, and status from a run that is cancelled part way is still saved, so updates that already landed are not forgotten.
- A saved login or password can now be removed with a Clear saved value button; a blank field still keeps the saved value.
- Provider replies are stripped of control characters and truncated before they reach the record status and the activity log.
- The repository manifest description matches the plugin description.
- Yandex PDD is marked as a legacy provider because Yandex has retired the PDD API. Existing records still load.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.19.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a dns icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature

## Security

- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer

- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

- Reorganize files

## Documentation

## Initial release

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.
